archetypes.name: env-isolation
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether implement timing/report paths can still inherit design workflow state through ambient env or legacy artifacts.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the plan’s proposed gating of workflow fallback on LARCH_TIMING_SKILL=design and the implement caller pins to LARCH_TIMING_SKILL=implement. Compare every shell and Python timing-report invocation in scope against the stated DESIGN_TMPDIR clearing/omission contract, including refresh and finalize paths. Look for gaps where polluted design env, stale run-flags, or legacy ledger rows could still affect implement reports despite the plan’s intent. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: report-schema-drift
archetypes.rationale: Targets inconsistencies between scanner, renderer, CLI, issue trimming, fixtures, and tests after removing implement workflow.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the report-tokens plan across scan, render, issue assembly, CLI forwarding, golden fixtures, and tests. Verify that implement loses workflow grouping everywhere while design remains byte-identical, and that retained schema fields such as timing JSON workflow_path are intentionally stable where promised. Hunt for mismatched labels, forgotten keyword threading, obsolete fixture assumptions, or tests that no longer validate the intended implement/design split. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stale-contracts
archetypes.rationale: Looks for retired HARD/SIMPLE contracts still implied by docs, script APIs, harness pins, or acceptance greps.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the proposed removal as a contract migration rather than a code deletion. Check whether docs, script markdown, structure tests, acceptance greps, and operator-facing prose all agree on which workflow concepts remain design-only and which implement concepts are retired. Pay special attention to renamed meanings such as issue-sizing SIMPLE versus workflow SIMPLE, and to places where tests intentionally retain legacy literals only for rejection coverage. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
